But I think it's less about what they meant to us and more about what they meant to everyone else. The first thing people do when they find a crashed plane is look for the life raft. The second thing is look for a map. The third thing is look for anything that looks familiar — because that's the clue that someone else has been here before and knows how to survive.

The flowers were that clue. They're a subtle, non-obvious sign that things are not normal out here. Someone came before us and found a way to live, and they left evidence of that.

That's why I'd go looking for them immediately if I were in your shoes. Not because it has any practical value — it doesn't. But because it's a symbol of a shared experience. That's a meaningful thing to know, even when you can't explain the why.
